Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as Mr. Deveshnath Tiwari, learned Additional Government Advocate, representing the respondent - State, and gone through the entire file.
2.

By way of this application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. the accused-applicant seeks bail,
apprehending his arrest in FIR/Case Crime No.0382 of 2022, under Section 7/13 Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, Police Station- Bisauli, District Budaun.

3. The prosecution case, as per the First Information Report lodged by Smt. Phoolwati on 30.7.2022 against the accused-applicant, is that she had given an application against her husband and in-laws regarding her harassment and second marriage of her husband which was registered as Case Crime No. 1 of 2019, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mahila Thana, District Budaun in which investigation had been concluded and charge sheet was submitted,
after which she told the accused- applicant who was the Investigating Officer of that case to add sections with regards to second marriage of her husband on which he demanded a bribe from her and threatened her and took Rs.8,000/- from her.

sentences.text: Fazal Khan, Giri and brother of the complainant went to the house of complainant where her husband Satendra, his second wife and her in-laws were present.

The accused-applicant recorded the statement of second wife of her husband and made a video on the spot after which the accused-applicant demanded Rs.5,000/- from the complainant for proceeding further with the matter, on which she expressed her inability, thereafter even not mentioning the fact regarding second marriage and not adding the relevant sections for it investigation concluded and charge sheet was submitted by the applicant.
The present F.I.R. thus was lodged.
4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant argued that the accused-applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is further argued that the present case has been lodged with malafide intentions as the accused-applicant had been the investigating officer of the case lodged earlier by the first informant/opposite party no. 2 as she was pressurizing the accused-applicant of doing some illegal act in that matter.
It is argued that the entire allegations levelled against the accused-applicant are concocted and with malafide intentions.
The applicant is having no criminal history as stated in para-23 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application.
It is further argued that the accused-applicant was granted interim protection vide order dated 15.12.2022 and charge-sheet has been filed.
There is no chance of tampering with the evidence or influencing the prosecution witnesss by the accused-applicant.
5. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the accused-applicant, this anticipatory bail application is hereby allowed.

The accused-applicant is directed to appear before the trial Court concerned within one week from today and if he does so, he shall be released on bail on his filing bail bond and two sureties, each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court,
if not already filed, on the following conditions, which are imposed in the interest of justice, and other conditions, which may be desirable by the learned trial Court:-
(i) the applicant(s) shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;

(ii). the applicant(s) shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;

(iii). in case, the applicant(s) misuse(s) the liberty of bail and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant(s) fail(s)
to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code; and (iv) the applicant(s) shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of Vijay Singh vs State Of U.P And Another on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62930531/
